title: Enterprise Onboarding — Integration, Escalation, Known Issues & QBR Playbook
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures used by Customer Success, Support, and SRE during enterprise customer onboarding and ongoing account health. It covers: integration checklist, escalation paths and runbooks, known issues and mitigation steps, support process and SLAs, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) health-check templates. The goal is to provide a repeatable, high-quality onboarding experience that protects production SLOs and accelerates time-to-value.

Audience

- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers / Integration Engineers
- Support Engineers (L1/L2/L3)
- Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
- Account Executives (for contract/cadence coordination)

Objectives

- Standardize integration steps so customers reach production readiness within target onboarding windows.
- Provide clear escalation tiers and runbooks to resolve incidents quickly.
- Maintain a living known-issues catalog with verified workarounds.
- Standardize QBR metrics and health checks for continuous improvement.

Roles & Ownership

- CSM: overall onboarding owner, coordinates QBRs and stakeholder communications.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): owns integration tasks (API keys, networking, sample prompts).
- Support L1: first responder for customer tickets; executes known workarounds.
- Support L2/L3: deeper triage, logs, and handoff to SRE or product.
- SRE: production incidents, capacity, and performance issues.

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (SE + CSM)

1. Contract & Account Setup
   - Verify signed contract and subscription type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
   - Confirm billing contact and billing behavior (usage vs. reserved).
2. Security & Network
   - Collect allowlist IPs for redwood-console & API endpoints: 52.27.10.0/24, 13.35.20.0/24 (example).
   - If Private/VPC: confirm VPN/IPsec details and KMS/HSM requirements.
3. Keys & Access
   - Generate API key with appropriate role (integration-se) in Console.
   - Grant temporary support access if requested (time-bound access via IAM).
4. Test Plan
   - Agree on smoke tests: sample generation, streaming, embeddings, and latency checks.
   - Define acceptance criteria: 95p latency < 400ms for 128 tokens on Hosted, no functional errors in 10k sample calls.

Integration Guide — Step-by-step

A. Environment preparation
- Required services: redwood-console, routing-proxy, model-ingestor, metrics-agent.
- Minimum firewall rules: outbound 443 to api.redwood.ai and console.redwood.ai.
- If using Dedicated: ensure dedicated-gpu-pool hostnames resolved via corporate DNS.

B. API Key & Test call
- Create API key in Console (Grant: call:generate, call:embed). Note key prefix: rwd_{8}.
- Sample curl: 

  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_XXXXXXXX" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rw-small", "input":"Hello world"}'

- Expected response: 200, JSON with field `output` and tokens metadata.

C. Network & Private Deployment Notes
- For Private deployments, confirm:
  - KMS endpoint accessibility (kms.customer.example:443)
  - TLS certs installed on router-proxy (Let'sEncrypt or customer CA)
  - Internal load balancer health check path: /healthz returning HTTP 200

D. Prompts, Rate Limits & Quotas
- Recommend rate-limit headers: X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining visible to clients.
- Initial quota recommendation for onboarding: 50 rps burst, sustained 10 rps for 48 hours.

E. Validation checklist (pass/fail tests)
- Tokenization parity check: sample text => token count within 2 tokens of SE reference.
- Latency checks: 95th p < target (see SLOs below).
- Correctness checks: no model hallucination on defined guardrail prompts.

Escalation Playbook

Severity definitions (customer-facing):
- P0 / Sev1 — Production outage: inference fails for >95% of requests or >5-minute sustained region outage. Response target: initial contact 15 minutes, mitigation or rollback within 60 minutes.
- P1 / Sev2 — Degraded production: significant errors or latency impacting majority of requests. Response target: initial contact 1 hour, resolution or mitigation within 4 hours.
- P2 / Sev3 — Functional impact to subset of requests or non-critical features. Response target: initial contact 4 hours, resolution within 3 business days.
- P3 — Informational / enhancement. Response within 3 business days.

Escalation contacts matrix (example)

- L1 Support: support@redwood.ai (first-touch)
- L2: oncall-support@redwood.ai (during business hours)
- SRE oncall: pagerduty SRE (P0/P1 escalations)
- Engineering (runtime): runtime@redwood.ai (for kernel/scheduling issues)

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Triage (L1) — Verify customer identity, collect request IDs, timestamps, sample payloads, and top-line error messages. Attach logs.
2. Reproduce (L1/L2) — Attempt to reproduce in staging or with a redacted customer payload. If reproducible, mark as actionable and escalate to L2.
3. Mitigate (L2/SRE) — Apply short-term mitigation: routing fallback to compatible model variant, enable prefix cache, or roll traffic to hosted fallback.
4. Resolve (SRE/Product) — Deploy fix or rollback, validate with test harness, and plan postmortem for P0/P1.
5. Communicate — Use the incident template (Appendix A) for status updates every 30 minutes for P0 and hourly for P1.

Runbook: High-latency token spikes

- Symptoms: 95p token latency > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes.
- Immediate steps:
  1. Check routing-proxy and queue length (metrics: routing_queue_length).
  2. If backlog > 500 requests, enable autoscale-burst (if on Dedicated) or route to regional fallback.
  3. If KV cache miss rate > 70%, investigate model variant mismatch.
  4. Notify SRE oncall and execute mitigation.

Known Issues & Workarounds (living table)

| Issue ID | Symptom | Impact | Workaround | Owner | Status |
|---------|---------|--------|-----------|-------|--------|
| KI-2026-014 | Intermittent streaming disconnects for large payloads (>16k chars) | Streaming clients drop mid-response, customer-visible partial output | Increase websocket ping interval, switch to chunked polling for large payloads; apply client-side buffer-retry (example snippet in Appendix B) | eng-serving-runtime | documented |
| KI-2026-021 | Tokenization mismatch for certain emojis in rw-tokenizer v2.1 | Slightly higher token usage and unexpected truncation | Pin tokenizer to v2.0 for affected customers; apply server-side normalization of input | applied-ml-and-evals | workaround_applied |
| KI-2026-033 | Dedicated pool noisy neighbor causing latency spikes | Elevated 95p latency on dedicated nodes | Move customer to alternate GPU pool or enable soft isolation; schedule capacity rebalancing | eng-sre | investigating |

For each known issue include: reproducible test case, telemetry query, and rollback steps. The canonical telemetry queries live in eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts.

Support Process & Ticketing

- Ticket intake: Zendesk for customer-facing tickets; internal triage in Jira (project: CS-SUPPORT).
- Required ticket fields: customer_id, environment (hosted/dedicated/private), API_key_suffix, sample_request_id, logs_attachment (max 10MB), severity.
- Triage workflow: L1 acknowledges within severity target window and attempts documented workarounds. If unresolved, escalate to L2 with logs and reproduction steps.

SLA targets (customer-facing)

- P0: initial response 15 minutes, status updates every 30 minutes, target mitigation within 60 minutes.
- P1: initial response 1 hour, updates hourly, mitigation in 4 hours.
- P2: initial response 4 hours, mitigation in 72 hours.

Health Checks & QBR Template

QBR cadence and owner
- Quarterly cadence owned by CSM with participation from SE and SRE for technical review.

Key metrics to review (minimum)
- Uptime: API success rate (5xx rate) — target > 99.9% monthly.
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency for main routes — target per-contract (example: <400ms for rw-medium on Hosted).
- Cost: tokens per active-user, monthly unit cost trend (handled by finance/CS).
- Model quality: failure rate on guardrail prompt set, regression delta vs baseline.
- Support: ticket volume by severity, mean time to first response, mean time to resolution.

QBR Agenda (example)
1. Executive summary & adoption metrics (CSM)
2. Reliability review: incidents since last QBR, root causes, mitigation status (SRE)
3. Integration health: API, network, auth, and validation results (SE)
4. Usage & cost trends (CSM + Finance)
5. Roadmap items and feature requests (Product)
6. Action items and next steps

QBR Artifacts & Deliverables
- One-page health dashboard PDF exported from Console.
- Action log with owners and due dates.
- Follow-up technical tasks opened in Jira (link in related_pages).

Appendix A — Incident Communication Template

- Subject: [P0] Customer X — Inference outage — <short description>
- Body:
  - Summary: timeline of issue start and current impact.
  - Impacted endpoints and customers.
  - Mitigation in place.
  - Next update ETA.
  - Owner and escalation contacts.

Appendix B — Example client-side retry snippet (node.js)

  const axios = require('axios');
  async function resilientGenerate(payload, key) {
    for (let i=0;i<3;i++) {
      try {
        const res = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', payload, {
          headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` }, timeout: 10000
        });
        return res.data;
      } catch (err) {
        if (i === 2) throw err;
        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500 * (i+1)));
      }
    }
  }

Appendix C — Useful queries and dashboards

- routing_queue_length: sum by pool over last 5m > 500 indicates backlog.
- model_latency_95: by model and pool.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: if <30% during steady-state, invalidate small keys.
